title: Software System for Perceptual Validation of Web Accessibility Based on Computer Vision and Optical Character Recognition
accessibility_issues: Perceptual readability of rendered text under simulated visual impairments (dichromacy, cataract, metamorphopsia): contrast, font size, overlap; information loss ratio.
main_contribution: Perceptual validation system: Selenium screenshots, OpenCV simulation of ophthalmological conditions and Tesseract OCR as an 'artificial observer'; words lost after simulation indicate barriers (information loss ratio) for CI/CD quality gates.
limitations: No empirical evaluation; OCR legibility assumed as a proxy for human perception (hypothesis not tested); OCR noise thresholds set empirically; visual impairments only; desktop viewport.
ground_truth_and_metrics: None (illustrative example on one page; no ground truth or metrics reported).

title: Webpage Accessibility Evaluation Using Machine Learning Technique
accessibility_issues: 41 WCAG 2.1 guidelines/checkpoints tested by MAUVE++ (pass, fail, cannot tell) on university homepages.
main_contribution: Decision Tree classifier over MAUVE++ JSON reports to classify checkpoint outcomes and compute an accessibility barrier score per webpage; case study of five Hungarian university homepages.
limitations: DT trained and tested on the tool's own outcomes (labels from MAUVE++), so near-perfect metrics are expected; five homepages; no comparison with the tool alone; expert check only qualitative.
ground_truth_and_metrics: MAUVE++ outcomes as labels; 10-fold CV (70/30); accuracy, precision, sensitivity, specificity and F1 per site (0.98-1.0); barrier scores 33.6-83.4; questionnaire with three experts (3-point scale, qualitative).

title: An Automated Framework for Proactive Accessibility Compliance in Enterprise Systems: Integrating AI-Augmented Testing, WAI-ARIA Patterns, and CI/CD Pipelines
ai_technique: Computer Vision; Deep Learning; LLM / Generative AI
ai_role: Issue detection; Test generation; Automatic remediation
accessibility_issues: WCAG 2.1/2.2 AA in enterprise .NET applications: 1.3.1, 1.4.3, 2.1.1, 2.4.7, 3.3.2, 4.1.2, 1.3.4, 2.5.8 (alt text, contrast, keyboard, focus, labels, ARIA).
main_contribution: Shift-left CI/CD framework combining rule-based scanners (axe-core, Pa11y, Lighthouse CI, linters), AI-based visual regression and semantic violation detection, AI-generated test scenarios, LLM remediation, a WAI-ARIA 1.2 component library and governance KPIs; 12-month case study at TMHP.
limitations: AI components described generically (models, data and accuracy not reported); effects attributed to the whole framework, not to AI; single organization, before/after without control; measurement of the metrics not detailed.
models: Not specified (deep-learning visual testing; GPT-based remediation agent; QyrusAI/Bedrock for test scenarios)
ground_truth_and_metrics: 12-month before/after at TMHP PEMS: violations per release 142 to 40 (-71.8%), remediation time 45 to 16 days, compliant user pathways 42% to 79.4%, help desk tickets 320 to 112/month; no ground truth for the AI components.

title: Implementing AI-driven Web Accessibility: WCAG 2.2 Features to Improve Usability for Users with Disabilities
accessibility_issues: WCAG 2.2 violations (alt text, contrast, keyboard operability, headings, forms) and 'Understandable' content (text simplification).
main_contribution: Prototype web system with an AI-based accessibility checker, adaptive content rendering (Transformer-based text simplification) and assistive features; before/after evaluation with users.
limitations: AI components described vaguely (the paper says the NLP model 'is likely a Transformer or a fine-tuned version of T5'); no details on training data, detection models or how compliance and accuracy were measured; ethical concerns (bias, privacy) only mentioned.
validation_method: User study; Comparison with static tools
ai_input: Source code/DOM; Images/alt text; Textual content
models: Not specified (Transformer/T5-like model for simplification; unspecified ML/CV detectors)
ground_truth_and_metrics: 150 participants with disabilities and 150 with web knowledge; WCAG 2.2 compliance +31%, task completion +33.6%, satisfaction +43.9%; AI vs manual error detection accuracy +25.6% (no ground truth described).

title: Conversational AI-Powered Multi-Agent System for Mobile Application Accessibility Compliance: A RAG-Enhanced Pipeline Design
ai_role: Support to the evaluation process; Recommendation of fixes
accessibility_issues: Mobile app accessibility against WCAG 2.1 and the Korean KS X 3253:2025 guidelines (iOS VoiceOver, Android TalkBack).
main_contribution: Dual-agent RAG pipeline: a Problem Analysis Agent that takes test results, code snippets or issue descriptions, retrieves the relevant guidelines and explains root cause, compliance implications, user impact and priority; a Solution Support Agent that generates platform-specific remediation code and validation guidance.
limitations: Design only, no implementation results or evaluation; depends on issues found by other tools or people; hallucination risk acknowledged; candidate models not yet chosen.
models: Candidates: Gemma-7B, Llama 3.1-8B, Qwen-14B, GPT-4o; SBERT/OpenAI embeddings for retrieval
ground_truth_and_metrics: None.

title: Leveraging AI and Machine Learning to Address ADA Non-Compliance in Web Applications: A Novel Approach to Enhancing Accessibility
ai_technique: Machine Learning; Deep Learning; NLP; Computer Vision
accessibility_issues: ADA/WCAG issues: missing alt text, keyboard accessibility, low contrast, non-captioned media, form labels, ARIA roles, headings, text complexity, focus traps.
main_contribution: AI/ML approach that crawls HTML/CSS/JS and combines rule-based and ML detection (decision trees, random forest, neural networks; CNNs for images; NLP for alt text and readability) with human-in-the-loop remediation suggestions.
limitations: Dataset, models and experimental setup described only generically; accuracy figures without per-model detail; validation partly relies on axe/WAVE; user study details (number of participants) not reported.
validation_method: Comparison with static tools; User study
ai_input: Source code/DOM; Images/alt text; Textual content; Runtime interaction
models: Decision tree; Random Forest; neural networks; CNN; NLP models (not specified)
ground_truth_and_metrics: Self-collected web pages (compliant and non-compliant); detection accuracy about 95% for common issues and 87% for complex ones (accuracy, precision, recall, F1 defined); post-fix checks with axe/WAVE; users with visual, cognitive and motor disabilities: tasks 30% more efficient, satisfaction +25%.

title: Leveraging GPT-4o to Evaluate the Usability and Accessibility of Flutter App Interfaces
accessibility_issues: Usability and accessibility issues in Flutter UI code (WCAG 2.1 and Apple HIG), plus potential app store policy violations.
main_contribution: Fuel (Flutter UI Evaluation using LLMs): web wrapper that prompts GPT-4o to assess Flutter source code (widget tree) for usability and accessibility issues and suggest fixes; developer study plus exit survey.
limitations: 15 screens and 15 developers from local startups; developers may lack accessibility expertise; static code only (no rendering or runtime); single LLM; generic vs structured prompts produce partly different issues.
ground_truth_and_metrics: 15 Flutter app screens; each issue rated by three developers (valid/invalid; fixes complete/partial/incorrect); e.g., 91 usability issues with 82% confirmed valid; agreement between generic and structured prompts reported (76% for usability, 57% for accessibility).

title: Enhancing Web Accessibility: Automated Detection of Issues with Generative AI
accessibility_issues: WCAG 2.2 success criteria that rule-based checkers miss or cover partially, especially those needing semantic understanding (e.g., meaningful alt text, use of colour, headings and labels).
main_contribution: GenA11y: extracts page elements related to each testable WCAG 2.2 success criterion and prompts a multimodal LLM (expert role, criterion explanation, failure examples) to detect violations; compared with five rule-based checkers.
limitations: False positives on some criteria (e.g., 1.1.1, 1.4.1); criteria needing runtime interaction not covered; cost per website; single LLM; recall measured on existing datasets that do not cover all criteria.
validation_method: Automated benchmark / Dataset; Comparison with static tools
ai_input: Source code/DOM; Rendered UI/screenshot; Images/alt text
ground_truth_and_metrics: Two existing datasets (including one with 142 pages) mapped to WCAG 2.2 criteria for recall; precision on real websites with manual checking; precision 94.5%, recall 87.61%; on 30 real websites on average 8 more violation types than IBM, QualWeb, axe-core, A11yWatch and WAVE combined; about 4.78 USD per website.

title: LADar: an LLM-based Tool to Detect Web Accessibility Violations
accessibility_issues: Nine WCAG 2.2 success criteria that need interaction or semantic judgement: 1.1.1, 1.4.1, 2.1.1, 2.1.2, 2.4.3, 2.4.7, 3.1.2, 3.2.1, 3.2.2 (keyboard traps, focus order, focus visible, language of parts, context changes).
main_contribution: LADar: agentic accessibility auditor that combines rule-based checks with an LLM that plans and executes interaction-driven tests on the rendered page (keyboard navigation, focus, screenshots before/after) and validates semantics (e.g., alt text quality).
limitations: Covers 9 of 86 criteria; limited annotated benchmark (custom pages for 4 criteria); real-world results partly checked by sampling; LLM cost and non-determinism; preliminary evaluation.
validation_method: Automated benchmark / Dataset; Comparison with static tools
ai_input: Rendered UI/screenshot; Runtime interaction; Source code/DOM
models: GPT-4o (planning, semantic and visual validation); GPT-4o mini (screenshot comparison)
ground_truth_and_metrics: W3C ACT test pages (5 criteria) and custom pages from WCAG failure techniques (4 criteria) with manually assigned outcomes; 18 real-world pages; compared with axe-core 4.11 and Lighthouse 12.8; e.g., SC 3.1.2: 50 of 51 real-world cases confirmed; sample of 30 of 119 cases reviewed for another criterion.

title: Audit Website Images with LLMs
ai_technique: LLM / Generative AI; Computer Vision; NLP
accessibility_issues: Images on websites (French RGAA image theme, aligned with WCAG 1.1.1): whether an image is informative or decorative and whether a text alternative is needed.
main_contribution: Browser extension and LLM-based pipeline that categorizes website images (diagram, illustration, logo, pictogram, text), describes them and compares the description with adjacent text to decide if a text alternative is required.
limitations: Small evaluation (30 images for description quality; a few images for classification); no comparison with a traditional audit yet; depends on a proprietary LLM.
validation_method: Expert review; None / Proof of concept
ai_input: Images/alt text; Rendered UI/screenshot; Textual content
models: Claude 3.7 Sonnet / Claude 4.5 (selected); nine LLMs compared for description (incl. GPT-5.1, Gemini, LLaMA, Mistral); earlier pipeline with YOLOv8, OCR and BERT similarity
ground_truth_and_metrics: 30 images (10 diagrams, 10 illustrations, 10 pictograms) scored by 7 annotators (0-1 scale) to select the description model; classification test where GPT-5 and Claude classified all test images correctly.

title: A Hybrid Light-AI-based Framework for Accessibility Validation
ai_role: Issue detection; Support to the evaluation process
accessibility_issues: WCAG criteria that rule-based checks cannot fully evaluate (e.g., target size and offset 2.5.8, label in name 2.5.3, meaningful content), with traceable evidence per criterion.
main_contribution: Lightweight-first hybrid framework for accessibility validation: rule-based checks by default and AI components (small language models, small multimodal models, vision models, graph representations, web agents) only where human-like judgement is needed; normative anchoring, deterministic traceable execution and evidential artifacts; human reviewer for complex cases.
limitations: Methodological framework illustrated by case studies; precision/recall figures only illustrative; no systematic benchmark yet.
ai_input: Source code/DOM; Rendered UI/screenshot; Runtime interaction
models: Phi-3-mini (SLM); Gemma 4 (SMM); YOLO-type vision models; Claude Sonnet 4.6; GPT-4o (web agent)
ground_truth_and_metrics: Illustrative case studies (e.g., small interactive elements detected on a screenshot); recall-oriented strategy with human review; no ground truth dataset.

title: From Accessibility to Reachability: LLM-Driven Contrastive Accessibility Testing for Android Apps
accessibility_issues: Workflow-level barriers for screen reader users in Android apps: non-interactive controls, navigation traps, improper focus order, navigation dead zones.
main_contribution: LLM-driven contrastive accessibility testing: a visual Normal User Agent completes a task and provides guidance; a TalkBack-driven Blind User Agent (approximate relocation, vicinity skimming) tries the same task; differences in reachability reveal accessibility defects.
limitations: Short paper; task scenarios designed manually; Android only; quantitative results limited; depends on parsing TalkBack output from system logs.
ai_input: Runtime interaction; GUI/accessibility tree; Rendered UI/screenshot
ground_truth_and_metrics: 15 popular Android apps (over 5 million downloads each) with realistic tasks on physical devices via ADB; defects identified per app in four categories; no comparison with existing scanners reported in detail.

title: An Assessment of LLM-Based Auditing and Validation for Web Accessibility
accessibility_issues: HTML validity errors that cause WCAG failures (e.g., unclosed tags, missing legend) and WCAG 2.1 AA issues on simple websites.
main_contribution: Assessment of LLMs for HTML validation and accessibility auditing, with a two-step prompt (audit, then verification of each detected issue) to reduce hallucinations, and support for producing correct, accessible code.
limitations: Small dataset (10 snippets and 2 student websites); results partly qualitative; hallucinations remain (about 15% for GPT-4o); LLMs recommended as aids, not standalone tools.
ground_truth_and_metrics: 10 invalid HTML snippets and 2 student websites, labelled by the authors; error detection and hallucination rates per model (e.g., GPT-4o hallucinated in about 15% of cases vs close to 50% for another model); verification step identification accuracy reported.

title: LLMs for Accessibility in Mobile Apps: Detection and Repair
ai_role: Issue detection; Issue classification; Recommendation of fixes
accessibility_issues: Android accessibility violations in XML layouts reported by Google Accessibility Scanner (e.g., missing content labels, touch target size, text contrast, spacing, missing alt text).
main_contribution: Empirical evaluation of three LLMs on detecting, categorizing and repairing validated accessibility violations in XML layout files of open-source Android apps.
limitations: Inconsistent detection across violation types; contextual misinterpretation; remediation quality limited; prompt sensitivity and output variability; Android XML only.
validation_method: Automated benchmark / Dataset; Comparison with static tools
ground_truth_and_metrics: Open-source F-Droid apps; Accessibility Scanner 2.4.1 results manually validated against XML (404 validated issues); detection rates per model and type (e.g., best model about 38% of 336 issues overall; per-type rates from about 5% to 51%).

title:
Leveraging Large Language Models for Sustainable and Inclusive Web
Accessibility
ai_role: Issue detection; Support to the evaluation process
accessibility_issues: Accessibility of dynamically generated tabular components (WCAG 2.1): missing scope attributes, redundant headers, feedback for asynchronous loading and errors.
main_contribution: Assessment of LLMs reasoning directly on frontend/backend source code (PHP, Angular, React, Vue) to anticipate accessibility violations in generated HTML, plus a second LLM stage that verifies issues (correct, redundant or hallucinated).
limitations: Limited to table components rather than full websites; many hallucinated or redundant violations; verification accuracy low for some models; student-developed components.
validation_method: Automated benchmark / Dataset; Comparison with static tools; Expert review
ground_truth_and_metrics: Tabular Accessibility Dataset (data descriptor REG-0516): dynamic content snippets and 25 Vue table implementations; each reported violation classified by the authors as correct, redundant or hallucination; verification accuracy GPT-4o mini 34%, Gemini 30%, o3-mini 79%.

title:
ScreenAudit: Detecting Screen Reader Accessibility Errors in Mobile Apps
Using Large Language Models
accessibility_issues: Screen reader accessibility errors in Android apps overlooked by rule-based checkers (labels, focus, element grouping, announcements, context).
main_contribution: ScreenAudit: traverses app screens with TalkBack's pipeline, collects metadata and speech transcripts and uses an LLM to identify screen reader accessibility errors; includes a formative study and an expert evaluation.
limitations: Coverage limited to screen-reader-focusable elements; inaccurate explanations in some cases; incomplete context understanding; cannot test app functionality; 14 screens.
validation_method: Expert review; Comparison with static tools
ai_input: GUI/accessibility tree; Runtime interaction; Rendered UI/screenshot
ground_truth_and_metrics: Six accessibility experts (one blind screen reader user) audited 14 app screens: 163 expert-identified errors; ScreenAudit coverage 69.2% (vs 31.3% for Accessibility Scanner), precision 71.3%; expert-based error dataset released.

title:
An empirical investigation of Large Language Models for automated
software compliance testing: Evidence from web accessibility
accessibility_issues: 39 WCAG 2 AA success criteria evaluated on isolated HTML snippets.
main_contribution: Large empirical evaluation of seven cost-effective LLMs for web accessibility conformance testing with three prompting strategies and five replications, compared with axe-core, Lighthouse and Pa11y; dual metric (real vs decision accuracy) and an interpretive framework of criterion amenability to LLMs.
limitations: Snippet-level evaluation may differ from full-page testing; non-determinism; per-criterion sample sizes vary; interpretive framework based on expert judgement, not validated; LLMs recommended for human-in-the-loop use.
validation_method: Automated benchmark / Dataset; Comparison with static tools
models: Seven LLMs from DeepSeek, Google and Qwen (best: deepseek-reasoner)
ground_truth_and_metrics: 384 W3C ACT test cases (39 SC); best accuracy 71.52% (example-based prompts; +8.2% average over basic prompts); tools 22.9-33.9% real accuracy and 22.9-44.4% decision accuracy; dataset published.

title: How an LLM Can Improve Automatic Web Accessibility Validation ?
accessibility_issues: WCAG techniques that current validators cannot check automatically, needing semantic and contextual judgement (e.g., descriptive page titles, headings and landmark structure, link and label meaning, ARIA roles).
main_contribution: Extension of an automatic validator (MAUVE++) with GPT-4o functions and prompting techniques for specific accessibility techniques that previously required manual checking.
limitations: Ten pages only; verification by one expert (an author); single LLM; only selected techniques.
ground_truth_and_metrics: 10 pages from highly visited sites (CNN, Microsoft, eBay, Google, Samsung, Weather, Fandom, Instagram, ...); results verified by an accessibility expert; overall effectiveness 92.4% (e.g., 89.5% for one technique).

title:
On the Interaction with Large Language Models for Web Accessibility:
Implications and Challenges
accessibility_issues: Accessibility of HTML forms, tables and images (labels, fieldset/legend, table headers, alt text).
main_contribution: Exploratory study of how ChatGPT can evaluate and correct the accessibility of HTML code, with a discussion of implications and challenges of developer-LLM interaction.
limitations: Qualitative examples only; no systematic dataset or metrics; single LLM; risk of overconfident or incorrect assessments.
ground_truth_and_metrics: Illustrative HTML examples (form, table, image) assessed and corrected by ChatGPT; no ground truth or metrics.

title:
AccessGuru: Leveraging LLMs to Detect and CorrectWeb Accessibility
Violations in HTML Code
ai_role: Issue detection; Issue classification; Automatic remediation
accessibility_issues: Web accessibility violations in HTML, organized in a taxonomy of syntactic, semantic and layout violations (42 violation types, aligned with axe rules and WCAG 2.1).
main_contribution: AccessGuru: combines an Axe-Playwright detector with an LLM-based semantic detector, and taxonomy-driven prompting to correct violations; new benchmark of real-world violations.
limitations: Corrected segments not yet reintegrated into full HTML documents; semantic correctness judged against human corrections; dependence on axe for syntactic/layout detection.
validation_method: Automated benchmark / Dataset; Expert review; Comparison with static tools
models: GPT-4 (main); Qwen2.5, Qwen-VL and Mistral-7B also used
ground_truth_and_metrics: Benchmark of 3,500 real-world violations (42 types); violation score decrease up to 84%; semantic corrections compared with human expert corrections; alignment with axe, WAVE and AChecker outputs.

title:
Turning manual web accessibility success criteria into automatic: an
LLM-based approach
accessibility_issues: Three WCAG success criteria that require manual checks: 1.1.1 Non-text Content, 2.4.4 Link Purpose (In Context), 3.1.2 Language of Parts.
main_contribution: LLM-based scripts (via LangChain) that evaluate WCAG ACT test cases for three manual success criteria, compared with automated evaluators.
limitations: Only three criteria and a limited set of test cases; different LLMs per criterion; results not generalizable to full pages.
validation_method: Automated benchmark / Dataset; Comparison with static tools
ai_input: Source code/DOM; Images/alt text; Textual content
models: GPT-3.5 (1.1.1); Claude (2.4.4); GPT-4 (3.1.2); Bard also tested
ground_truth_and_metrics: W3C ACT test cases for the three criteria; overall 87.18% detection by the LLM scripts; automated evaluators (e.g., AccessMonitor, Lighthouse) often missed or only warned.

title:
AI-Powered Accessibility: Evaluating the Role of Machine Learning in
Inclusive User Interface Design
accessibility_issues: Colour contrast / text readability (WCAG contrast ratio, APCA-oriented perceptual contrast); text elements of rendered pages
main_contribution: AdaptiveUI: Chromium extension that predicts per-element readability on the rendered DOM with a supervised model and recolours the foreground in real time when the score falls below a user-specific threshold; evaluated with visually impaired users.
limitations: Scope limited to colour contrast; model trained on a synthetic dataset with labels derived from WCAG thresholds and heuristics; branded or tightly designed interfaces may resist changes; user-side adaptation, the source is not fixed.
validation_method: User study; Automated benchmark / Dataset; Comparison with static tools
models: Random Forest regressor (text also mentions random forest or gradient boosting)
ground_truth_and_metrics: Synthetic colour/typography dataset, continuous readability score in [0,1] (WCAG thresholds + perceptual heuristics); MAE 0.062 and Pearson r = 0.87 on the validation set vs. rule-based WCAG contrast-ratio classifier; user study N = 52 (40 visually impaired, 12 sighted), baseline vs adaptive: task completion time, error rate, perceived readability.

title:
Towards Designing a Set of Usability and Accessibility Heuristics
Focused on Cognitive Diversity: An Exploratory Case Study with
Generative Artificial Intelligence
accessibility_issues: Usability and accessibility for people with cognitive disabilities: heuristic criteria mapped to WCAG 2.2 (including AAA) and W3C COGA guidelines.
main_contribution: U + A heuristics and U + A-index: an integrated usability/accessibility heuristic set for people with cognitive disabilities; ChatGPT generated the heuristic-WCAG and COGA-WCAG correspondences used to select the criteria; applied by experts to four websites.
limitations: GenAI use exploratory; LLM mappings validated only by random spot checks; expert evaluation only (no users); four websites in one domain, homepages only; index tied to a specific user profile.
ground_truth_and_metrics: Mappings: random spot check by the authors, no metric. Case study: authors' heuristic evaluation of 4 homepages (Viver Bell-lloc, Auria, Imserso, SeniorTIC) with pass/fail/NA; U-index, A-index and U + A-index per site.

title: On the Limits for Web Accessibility Evaluation Using AI Agents
accessibility_issues: Seven challenging WCAG 2.2 success criteria beyond code syntax, including 1.1.1, 1.2.5 Audio Description, 2.1.2 No Keyboard Trap and 2.3.2 Three Flashes (multimedia and interaction).
main_contribution: Comparison of chatbots, agentic browsers and multi-agent systems built with different models and frameworks for assessing challenging WCAG 2.2 criteria against expert evaluation.
limitations: Agentic browsers and MAS often failed to provide an assessment (57.4% and 42.6% on average) or simulated results; multimedia criteria remain out of reach; small set of criteria and pages.
ai_input: Rendered UI/screenshot; Runtime interaction; Source code/DOM
models: ChatGPT 5.2; Claude Sonnet 4.5; Gemini 3; Comet; Atlas; DeepSeek-V3.2, Llama4-Scout, gpt-oss-120b, GPT-4o with CrewAI, Smolagents, LangGraph
ground_truth_and_metrics: Expert manual evaluation as reference; best precision 0.73 (DeepSeek-V3.2 + LangGraph); best recall 0.78 and F1 0.70 (DeepSeek-V3.2 + Smolagents).

title: AugmentAble: Teaming Web Augmentation and LLMs for Instant Accessibility Improvements
accessibility_issues: Common WCAG issues on live pages (missing alternative text, insufficient contrast, unlabeled form elements).
main_contribution: AugmentAble: client-side web augmentation in which an LLM first evaluates a page's accessibility and then generates augmentation scripts to fix the reported issues, with local models for privacy.
limitations: Demo paper; no evaluation yet (usability study planned); user-side fixes do not change the source.
models: Local LLMs via Ollama; multimodal LLMs (e.g., Qwen-VL, AyaVision) for image descriptions
ground_truth_and_metrics: None (demonstration).

title: Towards Testing the Accessibility of Dynamic Visual Changes in Android Mobile GUI with Multi-Modal LLMs
accessibility_issues: Dynamic visual changes in Android GUIs (appearance/colour cues after interactions) that are not conveyed to blind screen reader users.
main_contribution: VisualDroid: multimodal LLM with a three-hop reasoning prompt that detects and classifies GUI visual changes and whether they are accessible to blind users; compared with image-based and dynamic-content baselines.
limitations: Android only; depends on exploration coverage; LLM cost and non-determinism; sub-problem of GUI accessibility (visual changes).
validation_method: Automated benchmark / Dataset; Comparison with static tools
ai_input: Rendered UI/screenshot; GUI/accessibility tree; Runtime interaction
models: GPT-4o (compared with CLIP, ViT, BLIP-2, GPT-4 Turbo for cost/efficiency)
ground_truth_and_metrics: Ground truth on 34 apps from 17 domains: F1 94.7%, above baselines (pixel similarity, spot-the-difference, TimeStump, Accessibility Scanner); five F-Droid apps: developers resolved three reported issues.

title: Expanding WCAG Success Criteria Testing Coverage with Browser-Native AI
accessibility_issues: WCAG success criteria beyond automated coverage that need semantic judgement (e.g., 2.5.3 Label in Name, 2.4.4 vague link text).
main_contribution: Hybrid browser extension combining axe-core static analysis, scoped context extraction and active browser simulation with the on-device small language model Gemini Nano to expand WCAG testing coverage with zero cost and local privacy.
limitations: Initial tests only; small model capacity; limited set of criteria and pages.
ground_truth_and_metrics: Initial tests: recall 84.6% (test set and number of criteria to be confirmed).

title: Accessibility By Design
accessibility_issues: WCAG 2.2 violations in HTML (assessment mode); generation of compliant code (develop mode).
main_contribution: Accessibility by Design research framework: SviluppAbile, a browser extension with a RAG pipeline grounded in WCAG 2.2 and W3C techniques that identifies potential violations, explains them and suggests fixes; plus a sonification suite for visual STEM content (not part of the testing scope).
limitations: Research proposal; tool under development; no evaluation yet; LLM hallucination acknowledged as the main risk (RAG and fine-tuning planned).
ground_truth_and_metrics: None yet; planned dataset of content-specific violations and comparison with traditional tools.

title: Bridging the Interpretation Gap in Accessibility Testing: Empathetic and Legal-Aware Bug Report Generation via Large Language Models
accessibility_issues: Violations reported by Google Accessibility Scanner (ATF) in Android apps: touch target size (64), content labeling (13), contrast ratio (26); narratives grounded in WCAG and Japanese regulation (JIS X 8341-3:2016).
main_contribution: HEAR (Human-cEntered Accessibility Reporting): turns raw scanner bug reports into persona-based, legally aware narratives (UI context reconstruction from screenshot and view hierarchy via semantic slicing and visual grounding; disability persona injection; chain-of-thought on physical barrier, functional blockage and legal risk).
limitations: Depends on the upstream scanner and inherits its false positives; 3 violation types, 4 apps; static single-disability personas (stereotype risk); hallucination judged by the authors; user study with 12 university participants; comparison with raw logs confounded by information density; single LLM.
ground_truth_and_metrics: 103 violations from 4 Android apps (Instagram, Wish, Teams, Booking; 4 screens each). RQ1: two authors rated each report pass/fail on visual grounding, textual fidelity and functional logic (hallucination if any fails); no hallucinations, no disagreements. RQ2: user study N = 12, HEAR vs raw scanner logs (empathy, urgency, persuasiveness, legal-risk awareness, cognitive load; preference by task).

title: Optimising web accessibility evaluation: Population sourcing methods for web accessibility evaluation
accessibility_issues: Selection of representative web pages for accessibility evaluation (WCAG-EM sampling), with accessibility measured by axe.
main_contribution: Framework complementing WCAG-EM that measures population-sourcing methods (e.g., server log files and crawling) and clusters heterogeneous pages with unsupervised learning to select representative samples (coverage, representativeness, complexity, popularity, freshness, accessibility).
limitations: Few websites; clustering quality depends on templated development and features; accessibility indication limited to an automated tool; DBSCAN may produce large heterogeneous clusters.
models: DBSCAN on a dimensionality-reduced vector-space model of pages; K-Means for re-clustering
ground_truth_and_metrics: Populations of real websites (e.g., 1,329 and 991 pages; 9,462 pages in 50 clusters); metrics of coverage, representativeness and accessibility (axe violation severities) across sampling methods.

title: VisionAlt-Score: Large-Scale Automated Quality Grading of Web alt Text Attributes
accessibility_issues: Quality of image alt text (WCAG 1.1.1): missing, vague, generic or mismatched descriptions.
main_contribution: VisionAlt-Score: metric combining CLIP image-text alignment with heuristic penalties for very short or generic strings and diminishing returns for long descriptions; applied at web scale.
limitations: Not validated against human or screen reader user judgements (planned); CLIP alignment is a proxy for usefulness; heuristic weights set by the author.
ground_truth_and_metrics: 80,000 image-text pairs sampled from the public web; score distributions by description length and website type; no human ground truth.

title: Towards developing a framework for automated accessibility evaluation of web content from expert perspectives
accessibility_issues: Fifteen accessibility criteria obtained from web experts and researchers (content and user-perspective aspects beyond tool checks).
main_contribution: Framework for automated accessibility evaluation of web content from expert perspectives: identification of criteria with experts, evaluation of each criterion with AI techniques (mainly NLP and auxiliary algorithms), and validation on webpages plus a questionnaire-based user study.
limitations: Small number of webpages (Hungarian sites); AI techniques described generally; questionnaire validation only; PDF text layer is garbled (reading from a partly corrupted extraction).
models: Not specified (NLP methods and auxiliary algorithms)
ground_truth_and_metrics: Experimental evaluation on Hungarian webpages; questionnaire with users comparing the framework's results on the same 15 attributes (percentages per rating).

title: Computation of Accessibility Score of Educational Institute Webpages using Machine Learning Approaches
accessibility_issues: Accessibility of university homepages assessed on ten aspects aligned with WCAG, combining automated tool results (e.g., Validator, MAUVE++, WAVE) into a custom dataset.
main_contribution: Computation of accessibility scores for Hungarian university homepages with Random Forest and Decision Tree classifiers on a custom dataset, plus a questionnaire analysis.
limitations: Custom small dataset; labels derived from tool outputs; few webpages; PDF text layer garbled.
ground_truth_and_metrics: Custom dataset of Hungarian university homepages; accuracy, precision, sensitivity, specificity and F1 per classifier; questionnaire with participants.

title: An AI Solution for Web Accessibility and Images Classification
accessibility_issues: Website images under the French RGAA image theme (WCAG 1.1.1): informative vs decorative images and need for text alternatives.
main_contribution: AI workflow for an automatic accessibility audit of website images: image category classification (CNN, YOLO) as the first step to decide informative vs decorative images and generate alt text for informative ones.
limitations: Initial experiments only; class imbalance (good recall for pictograms, low for other classes); full workflow not yet evaluated end to end.
ground_truth_and_metrics: Image classification experiments with accuracy, precision, recall and F-score (e.g., about 0.93 recall and precision for the pictogram class).

title: Method and Algorithm for Web Content Analysis Based on Computer Vision for Contrast Evaluation
accessibility_issues: Text-background contrast on rendered web pages (WCAG 1.4.3 contrast ratios), for users with visual impairments.
main_contribution: Method and software module that analyses screenshots with OpenCV and Tesseract OCR to locate text blocks and compute text-background contrast without access to the source code.
limitations: OCR errors on complex backgrounds; colour detection inaccuracies; sequential processing (addressed in REG-1619); limited evaluation.
ground_truth_and_metrics: Not reported in detail (functional demonstration on web pages).

title: Parallelization and Optimization of a Method for Web Content Analysis and Accessibility Evaluation for Visually Impaired Users
accessibility_issues: Text contrast in images of web content according to WCAG 2.1.
main_contribution: Optimized and parallelized version of the screenshot-based contrast analysis method (preprocessing, region-specific OCR, parallel processing of text blocks, improved colour detection).
limitations: Focus on performance; accuracy gains small; OCR limitations on large or textured images; same group's companion method (REG-1582).
ground_truth_and_metrics: Image dataset of varying sizes: processing time and text recognition/contrast accuracy (e.g., recognition accuracy improved from 92.5% for small images; overall +1.2-3.4%).

title: AI-Powered Real-time Accessibility Enhancement: A Solution for Web Content Accessibility Issues
accessibility_issues: Missing ARIA landmarks, ill-formed headings, low contrast text, inadequate form labels, missing alt text.
main_contribution: AI-enabled system injected into pages (Page Scanner and DOM Renderer) that sends the rendered DOM and a screenshot to a server where pretrained image classifiers, CLIP and a fine-tuned GPT-3.5 model identify issues and return fixes applied in real time.
limitations: Case studies on sample pages only; no quantitative evaluation; runtime fixes on the client; security and reliability concerns mentioned.
ai_input: Source code/DOM; Rendered UI/screenshot; Images/alt text
models: Fine-tuned GPT-3.5; CLIP zero-shot image classifier; pretrained image classifiers
ground_truth_and_metrics: Case studies on sample web pages accessed locally; before/after illustrations; no metrics.

title: A transformer-based deep learning model for evaluation of accessibility of image descriptions
accessibility_issues: Accessibility of image descriptions (alt text/captions) measured as compliance with ten NCAM image description guidelines (relates to WCAG 1.1.1).
main_contribution: Transformer-based deep learning model that predicts compliance of a given image description with ten NCAM accessibility guidelines.
limitations: Trained and tested on Flickr8k captions, not on descriptions collected from websites or apps; unbalanced labels; some guidelines with poorer results.
ground_truth_and_metrics: Flickr8k image descriptions labelled by experts for the 10 NCAM guidelines; precision, recall, F1 and AUC-PR per guideline (values around 0.9 for most guidelines).
